title: Hardware, transport, worker, and reproduction probes

sources.notes: Models backend admission, pre-capture and post-replay oracle checks, graph replay ordering and per-backend failure recording. The float64 reference is CUDA-resident, not a CPU implementation; projections, routing, transport, scheduling and HTTP are excluded.

Models one CUDA-mapped allocation containing signal/completion, captured WRITE-then-WAIT ordering, CPU polling and completion publication. A five-second signal timeout ends measurement but still permits return zero.
Models independently mapped flag pages and synchronized GPU write followed by CPU sweep/prefix scans. This is host scan cost, not concurrent doorbell detection; zero layer count is not validated.
Models identical H2D-kernel-D2H submissions observed by blocking SYCL wait, SYCL status polling, or native zeEventQueryStatus. Native-handle failure omits that arm and all polling is unbounded.

Models split versus fused host-to-device submissions and event-status completion. It times a kill hypothesis but does not validate bytes; ids and weights are uninitialized and only a kernel prefix is written.

Models SBINT401 plane extraction, provider load/issue/take, deterministic two-layer dispatch and same-bank float64 CPU oracle with peak-relative threshold. Exceptional paths do not guarantee provider teardown.

The tracked .cpp object is entirely NUL bytes and contains no declarations or executable behavior. It is an explicit contradiction/artifact boundary, not evidence for a B70-to-B70 dma-buf control path.

Models pointer-only native kernel binding and a fixed closed WAIT-reset-kernels-D2H-completion list, including timeout and bit-exact SYCL-reference observation. No per-submit command-list patching occurs.

Models shipped baked kernel handles and mixed pointer/u32 bindings against the split SYCL result, plus optional foreign CUDA-pinned H2D/D2H plumbing. Missing CUDA runtime skips only the foreign-host stage.

Models a temporary one-row SBEXP001 bank, captured-route compaction, provider dispatch, health and nonfinite observations, immutable digests and finally-protected shutdown. It has no numerical oracle.
Models XPU availability and timed GEMMs only. The claimed reference remains on XPU, no numerical threshold is enforced, and PASSED is printed unconditionally after available-device execution.

Models zex WAIT/WRITE acceptance, submit-before-ring ordering, host release-store and optional CUDA-DMA ringing. CUDA timeout performs a host rescue so timeouts can still end with process status zero.

Models real provider/poller ABI setup, 47 registered pinned lanes, serial/burst publication, explicit CS arming, wedge replay, signal scrubbing, error accounting and normal stop/destroy. Internal list construction/patching belongs to the provider library.

Models distinct launch/copy/environment/graph/persistent/queue modes. Default all omits several modes and unknown modes return success; the INT4 graph branch uniquely compares eager replay and a host CPU reference.
Models two disjoint provider/poller lanes, CUDA issue-all-before-take-all graph ordering, same-bank CPU oracles, card-isolation sentinels, replay stress, error counters and lane teardown.
Models serial, dual in-order and out-of-order dependency chains, endpoint payload checks and an overlap ratio verdict. Timing work buffers are uninitialized and not numerical outputs.

Models controller-owned shared-memory sequence handoff and output completion. Contrary to its name it never calls the imported ESIMD module, ignores routed expert IDs and runs positional Torch FP16 matmuls.

Models synthetic oneMKL MoE timing and printed CPU comparison. The CPU side reuses expert-0 weights for routes 0/1/2 and PASS/CHECK never changes exit status, so it is not an enforced multi-expert oracle.

Models uncached resident-device polling, system-scope acknowledgement, x86 flush/fence publication, abort/guard status and idle/contended arms. A failed busy allocation weakens the contended arm without refusing it.
Models per-card/concurrent bandwidth, touched device residency, Linux memory accounting and pageable CPU commitment. Discovery/cleanup limitations and nonfatal allocation refusal remain explicit.
Models solo asymmetry, concurrent shared-uplink contention, peer capability query and opt-in peer copy, plus the host-mediated baseline. Fewer than two devices returns success without a test.

Models grouped benchdnn correctness/performance invocation. The commented ref-implementation disqualifier is not enforced and lack of set -e permits an earlier failed pipeline to be masked by the final pipeline.
Models synchronous pinned-host H2D/D2H sweep and link-band diagnosis. Generic device selection and invalid iteration counts limit hardware identity and statistics.
Models synthetic profiling and serialized dispatch timing. No output is checked; the nominal fused gate/up phase derives both operands from the same expression.
Models zex operations appended to a SYCL-owned immediate list and the load-bearing CCS marker after a possibly BCS D2H. A native command-queue handle is explicitly unavailable for this experiment.
Models declaration-order binding of two pointers and three u32 values and exact output comparison. Native API failures are mostly diagnostic and become fatal only when output differs.
Models controller-owned shared-memory sequence publication, routed random-weight Torch XPU compute, output copy and matching completion. It has no timeout, input bounds, atomics or numerical oracle.

Models real provider/poller registration arms, deterministic repeated dispatch, epsilon replay stability, health/error counters and trace timing. It compares registered versus unregistered staging, not CPU numerical output.
Models controller/worker shared-memory sequencing and overlap timing. CPU, CUDA and worker weights are unrelated, B70 output is not combined, and early worker death can skip normal cleanup.
Models CUDA VRAM dma-buf export, Level Zero import, full-pattern B70 write provenance, copy/compute-engine timing and pinned-host comparison. Failures are stage-labelled killed outcomes.
Models synchronized throughput for NVFP4, MXFP4 and FP16 storage through one grouped kernel. Operands differ, output is unchecked, and caught per-case failures do not make main fail.

Self-contained oneAPI build harness for device_usm_host_shadow.cpp; shell has no declared function symbols. It conditionally sources setvars and compiles with icpx -fsycl, but contributes no runtime probe behavior.

Models retained optional-touched device-USM chunks and system MemAvailable/MemFree versus process RSS. Non-divisible remainder is ignored and the after-free sample still occurs before queue/context destruction.

Models repeated retained device allocation plus synchronized memset across externally selected adapter/queue modes. Null allocation breaks early but still prints PASS, yielding the modeled requested-versus-completed false-pass witness.
Models exact converted INT4 layout checks, eight-route same-fixture CPU oracle with FP16 boundaries, cosine/MAE gates, warmed latency and finally-protected provider shutdown.
Models the smallest immediate-list 4-KiB CUDA-pinned-host to Intel-device copy and fail-fast API lifecycle. It validates API completion, not bytes.
Models immediate-list CUDA-device/pinned-host/B70 bounce and per-leg timing. Several sources are uninitialized and no content is checked; fixed enumeration arrays risk overflow.
Models regular command-list reset/append/close/execute per cross-vendor pinned bounce plus four-leg timing. Success is API retirement; B70 output has no producer and payload is unchecked.
Models immediate-list successor with copy-group preference, one host sync for the timed L0 pair, individual leg timing and cleanup. Device labels are not enforced and bytes remain unchecked.
Models B70 dma-buf export, CUDA opaque-fd import/pull, full-word provenance, pinned-host comparator and stage-labelled survival. Resource lifetime is largely process exit.

Models warmed memfd registration, fd/eventfd handoff, CUDA production and go/done reuse, plus private-pinned D2H reference. Full-route timing includes process and three PCIe copies; no payload is checked.

Models cold memfd creation, portable CUDA registration, deterministic device fill, synchronized D2H, fd transfer and lifetime through provider ack. Ack status/value is ignored and there is no timeout.
Models warmed provider fd/eventfd ownership, mapped-host H2D/D2H completion and done publication. It performs no payload validation; both nominal private reference event paths submit H2D.

Models cold ordinary mmap of received memfd, Level Zero H2D/D2H, sparse page-start verification, ack and teardown. It intentionally does not externally import the anonymous memfd and can block the host indefinitely on early failure.

assumptions: Probe models are qualification workflows, diagnostics and reproducers; they are not silently promoted into the production serving path.
Bounded counts 1 through 4 stand for concrete scenario fixtures, not production tensor sizes, layer counts, repetitions or proof over those ranges.
CUDA, SYCL, Level Zero, XPU, zex, dma-buf, IOMMU, cache coherence and timing effects are atomic external observations whose truth requires the named runtime and physical hardware.
A completion flag, event, sequence or successful API return does not imply valid bytes or numerical parity; those observations remain separate.
Generic, first-device or name-substring selection does not qualify an RTX 5090 or B70 unless the source explicitly checks it.
Unbounded source spins require external forward progress and are not liveness guarantees in this model.
Process-exit resource reclamation in dma-buf and diagnostic programs is represented as an experiment boundary, not reusable lifecycle quality.
The tracked b70_b70_dmabuf_control.cpp object is zero-filled and provides no behavior or symbols.
Pinned-staging files are scratch illustrations, not the qualified Phase-2 ring; their completion and timing claims exclude retries, backpressure and robust failure handling.
Performance outputs are deployment-specific measurements, not invariant throughput, latency, link width, overlap, or SLO claims.

implementation_checks.description: CPU-executable differential for exact converted quantized layout and scale values, followed by the same eight-route fixture through a CPU dequantized SwiGLU oracle with FP16 boundaries; hardware dispatch remains optional external evidence.

Using a small extracted SBINT401 fixture, compare the source CPU float64 dequantize/SwiGLU/weighted accumulation against retained expected arrays before requiring actual-provider parity on qualified hardware.

CPU-inspect and full-byte checksum the mapped deterministic pattern before H2D and full readback after D2H; compare with the current sparse page-start check to expose within-page corruption the source can miss.

Add a CPU memcpy/checksum measurement over the same shared and private pinned buffers to establish a host-memory floor and localize page/cache/process overhead without calling it peer-to-peer bandwidth.

Repeat the same chunked allocate-touch-retain-free lifecycle with anonymous CPU memory while sampling MemAvailable and RSS, distinguishing ordinary Linux commitment from device-driver buffer-object backing.

Source-inspect and record requested versus actually completed allocations so early null allocation cannot be classified as a full pass; CPU allocation can distinguish generic exhaustion but cannot adjudicate the Level Zero adapter defect.

At small seeded shapes, decode each storage format on CPU and compare grouped-GEMM outputs using identical logical weights/activations; keep throughput runs separate because the present random fixtures are not numerical equivalents.

Exercise the existing deterministic CPU reference against eager and captured stable-address INT4 graph results, including host-input mutation between replays and the documented static M=1 capture bound.
Source-inspect that the current reference tensors stay on XPU and that no threshold gates PASSED; a genuine CPU comparison must explicitly transfer seeded inputs and compute the reference on CPU.
